title: Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators Beyond Lindblad
authors: Elisa Vallini, Felix Fritzsch, Pieter W. Claeys
abstract: Out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) provide a powerful probe of quantum chaos and scrambling. While the Lindblad formalism is often used to describe OTOCs in open systems, microscopic mechanisms that give rise to the Lindblad equation at the level of time-ordered correlation functions do not necessarily justify this approach at the level of OTOCs. Starting from a microscopic model of a subsystem coupled to a random bath, we show that the resulting OTOC dynamics contains an additional contribution compared to the standard Lindblad approach. This contribution, induced by correlations between different replicas, allows key properties of the underlying unitary dynamics such as long-time freeness to be retained and information scrambling to be captured more faithfully. As an application, we show that this extended formalism can be used to numerically study OTOCs in large closed systems by replacing part of the system with a dissipative boundary, offering a way to study operator spreading and higher-order correlations beyond directly accessible system sizes.
summary: This paper develops an extended formalism for calculating Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs) in open quantum systems, showing that the standard Lindblad approach is insufficient. By including a crucial 'replica-correlation term,' the authors restore physical properties lost in the reduced description. This allows for more accurate study of quantum chaos and operator spreading in realistic, dissipative environments.
main_problem: The paper investigates Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs) in open quantum systems, specifically addressing the limitations of using the standard Lindblad formalism for these higher-order correlators.
main_result: The full OTOC dynamics requires an additional 'replica-correlation term' beyond the standard Lindblad approach, which restores fundamental properties like the conservation of the operator Hilbert–Schmidt norm.
method: The authors derive the OTOC evolution by systematically tracking correlations between environment replicas, leading to an extended formalism that corrects the standard reduced dynamics.
model_or_system: The study uses a microscopic model of a system coupled to a random bath, exemplified by a dissipative Ising chain with boundary dissipation. The dynamics are analyzed by comparing the full unitary evolution to the reduced Lindblad evolution.
key_observables: Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs), operator spreading, and the conservation of the operator Hilbert–Schmidt norm.
important_parameters: Dissipation strength ($\gamma$), time ($t$), and the replica number ($k$).
main_assumptions: The standard Lindblad formalism is insufficient for OTOCs because it neglects correlations between replicas, necessitating the inclusion of the replica-correlation term.
figures_summary: Figures compare OTOCs for different dissipation strengths ($\gamma$), showing that the full OTOC retains unitary-like behavior, while the reduced OTOC exhibits premature decay near the dissipative boundary.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the failure of the standard Lindblad approach for OTOCs to deriving the necessary replica-correlation term, and finally applying this extended formalism to study operator spreading in dissipative spin chains.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical tool to accurately calculate quantum chaos measures (OTOCs) in realistic open quantum systems, bridging the gap between unitary and dissipative dynamics.

The OTOCs are numerically studied for A = σz i , with i = 1, . . . , L, and B = σz 1, for a system of size L = 8. Panel (a) shows the OTOC under unitary dynamics, while panels (b) and (c) show the reduced and full OTOCs, respec- tively, for two different values of γ ̸= 0. The competition be- tween unitary scrambling and dissipation manifests differently in the two quantities, with the full OTOC ⟨A(t)BA(t)B⟩L providing a more faithful description of the scrambling dy- namics of the corresponding closed system.

FIG. 3. Correlation functions and OTOCs in the boundary- dissipated Ising chain (11), for boundary operators A = B = σz 1. (a) Correlation function for the open system (L = 8, γ = 1, dashed magenta), compared with the ones of the closed system for L = 14 (solid black) and L = 8 (solid gray). (b) Full OTOC for the open system (L = 8, γ = 1, dashed magenta), compared with the corresponding closed- system OTOCs for L = 14 (solid black) and L = 8 (solid gray). The reduced OTOC of the open system is also shown (dash-dotted blue). In both panels, the open-system results closely reproduce those of the larger closed system, whereas the reduced OTOC provides a significantly poorer approxi- mation.
